observations:
Torah #50 is structurally among the most compact Torahs in the dataset: 10 bechina edges, 13 nodes, 3 raw components, 2 final packages. The teaching has a single tight argument built entirely around the binary opposition of covenant-violation (evil) and covenant-keeping (good). Every concept in the Torah belongs either to the evil domain of פגם הברית (Package 1) or the good domain of שמירת הברית (Package 2).

A new package would require 3+ concepts with explicit bechina language forming an independent thematic domain not already captured by the two existing packages. No such domain was found.

Candidate clusters examined and rejected:

1. PRAYER (תְּפִלָּה) — Prayer is the arena in which the covenant-violation/keeping manifests, but the Rebbe does not use bechina language to equate תפלה to another concept in this Torah. It is the outcome that flows from the covenant domains via eitza, not a third parallel set of aspects. A prayer-package would be built on eitza connections (cause-and-effect) rather than bechina (shared nature), which the framework prohibits.

2. BONES / PRAYER-OF-BONES cluster (עֶצֶם, אַרְיֵה, כָּל עַצְמוֹתַי תֹּאמַרְנָה) — After adding the gap node כל עצמותי תאמרנה (torah_50_additions.json), this becomes a 3-node cluster, which meets the minimum count. However, these three nodes are not structurally independent of Package 2 — they are specific expressions of the positive side of covenant-keeping. The Rebbe presents כל עצמותי תאמרנה as the name for the state produced by having מיין מתיקין/מיין דדכין (pure waters = holy seed = guarding the covenant). The bones-and-lion sub-cluster deepens Package 2 but does not represent a domain with a different essential nature. Separating it into a new package would require an eitza-type justification (they result from pure-waters) rather than a bechina separation — which the framework explicitly forbids. Package 2's essential nature is the holiness of covenant-keeping; the bones and lion are aspects of that same holiness expressed in prayer and divine acceptance.

3. DOG cluster (כַּלְבָּא, עַזֵּי פָנִים) — After adding the two gap nodes from torah_50_additions.json, this would be a 2-node sub-cluster within Package 1, still below the 3-node threshold for a new package. Furthermore, these nodes are aspects of the same evil domain of covenant-violation (כלבא = מיין מרירין, עזי פנים = כלבים). They do not form an independent domain — they are human and metaphorical expressions of Package 1.

Structural summary of Torah #50's argument:

  [Package 2: good]         →eitza→   [Package 2: good]         →eitza→   prayer accepted
  שמירת הברית                          עצם / כל עצמותי תאמרנה              (lion eats sacrifice)
  מיין מתיקין / מיין דדכין             אריה
  זרע קדש / תקון הברית

  vs.

  [Package 1: evil]         →eitza→   prayer blocked
  פגם הברית                            (dog eats sacrifice)
  מיין מרירין / מיין מסאבין
  זרע טמא / מרה / חרב פיות / גיהנם

Good/evil mirror structure: Torah #50 has the most symmetrical mirror in the dataset. Every Package 1 node has a direct Package 2 counterpart:
  - מיין מרירין (bitter waters)   ↔   מיין מתיקין (sweet waters)
  - מיין מסאבין (defiled waters)  ↔   מיין דדכין (pure waters)
  - זרע טמא (impure seed)         ↔   זרע קדש (holy seed)
  - מרה (bitterness/Mara)         ↔   תקון הברית (covenant-repair)
  - חרב פיות (double-edged sword) ↔   [no exact counterpart — the sword is the absence of the lion's protection]
  - גיהנם (Gehinnom)              ↔   [no exact counterpart — Gehinnom is the far end of the evil pole]
  - כלבא (dog, gap node)          ↔   אריה (lion)
  - עזי פנים (brazen-faced, gap)  ↔   [implicit: the holy people whose prayer is accepted]

Conclusion: Torah #50 is a two-package Torah with complete good/evil polarity symmetry. No third package is warranted by the bechina structure or the thematic content of the teaching.
